caption: The drawing depicts a square piece of material, likely leather, decorated with a series of intricate geometric and curvilinear patterns. The artwork shows the lower left corner of this rectangular object, with the remainder extending outside the frame. The dominant colors are earthy brown and tan, accented with white or cream lines. The border on the left and bottom edges is solid brown, punctuated with evenly spaced round holes. Inside the border, there are multiple bands with repeating geometric designs: one band has a wavy line, and another is filled with a pattern of interlocking triangles or diamonds, while others feature small grid-like or cross-hatched motifs. In the upper right quadrant, the decoration becomes more complex, showing a wide band with an interlacing loop pattern bordered by fine lines and inset with small diamond or cross-shaped elements. The overall composition assembles these elements in nested right angles, creating a layered effect within the square format. The names “EDWARD JEWETT” and “R. Wm R. TAYLOR” are inscribed in small letters in the lower right corner. The background is plain and off-white, and there are no additional objects or features outside the decorated material.
